2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for the State as well as respondent No.2.
3.
The case of the prosecutor is that the complaint was filed by the mother of the victim on 08.05.2024 alleging that she herself, her husband and family members reside in the said address.
The elder daughter the victim, NC: 2024:KHC-K:6843 who is aged 16 years, slept along with her grandmother on the night of 07.05.2024 and in the morning of 08.05.2024, she was not found.
They traced all the places, but, they did not find her.
Hence, they filed the complaint suspecting that the petitioner had abducted the victim girl.
The police registered the FIR.
Thereafter, the father of the petitioner surrendered the petitioner before the police on 13.05.2024.
Accordingly, he was remanded judicial custody.

His bail petition came to be rejected by the Trial Court in Crl.Misc.
No.284/2024 vide order dated 20.06.2024.
Hence, he is before this court seeking regular bail.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the police have not arrested the petitioner.
The father of the petitioner brought and surrendered him before the police on 13.05.2024 and he is in custody for more than three months.
The investigation is completed and the charge sheet has been filed.
The petitioner is ready to abide any condition, that hon'ble Court may impose.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader has seriously objected petition contending that the victim is a minor girl aged 16 years.
During the investigation, it is revealed that she was subjected to the sexual assault by the petitioner.
He has abducted her and went to the Hyderabad with her and kept her in the house of his friend.
There the petitioner has committed sexual assault on the victim/minor girl.
Therefore, she prays for dismissing the petition.
6. Having heard the arguments and perusing the records, which would go to show that of course the age of the victim is 16 years.
The petitioner said to have called her by phone and she went along with the petitioner and stayed in Hyderabad
. During their stay in Hyderabad, the petitioner said to have sexually assaulted her.
Later, father of the accused took them to the police station and surrendered the petitioner.
Even if, the victim girl had given consent, her consent is immaterial since she is a minor girl.
The petitioner took the minor girl away from her lawful guardians and had sexual intercourse with her, NC: 2024:KHC-K:6843 which attacks Section 376 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 POSCO Act.
However, the investigation is completed and the charge sheet has been filed.
Custody of the petitioner is no more required for the purpose of any investigation.
Therefore, keeping him in jail will not serve any purpose.
The petitioner is said to be the permanent resident of the said address and by imposing certain conditions, if the bail is granted, no prejudice would be caused to the case of the prosecution.
